findings.title: ShinyHunters claims FBI hack, data theft in PeopleSoft zero-day breach
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported that ShinyHunters claimed it breached FBI systems using a new Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day. The article was later updated to include a statement from the FBI.

findings.title: Dutch 'reformed hacker' arrested in ShinyHunters hacking investigation, police say
findings.summary_md: Reuters reported that Dutch police arrested a 24-year-old suspect in the ShinyHunters investigation and that he was due to appear in a Rotterdam court. The report said a former boss identified the suspect as former hacker Pepijn van der Stap.

findings.title: ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft detained in Jordan, cooperating with bureau, sources say
findings.summary_md: Reuters reported that a suspected ShinyHunters member was detained in Jordan this week and was cooperating with the FBI, according to three sources. The group had said it stole data on every FBI employee after claiming responsibility for defacing the FBI website the previous month.

findings.title: Suspected ShinyHunters hacker detained in Jordan, cooperating with FBI, sources say
findings.summary_md: CBS News reported that Jordanian authorities detained Saif al-Din Khader and that ShinyHunters had claimed, without public verification, to hold data on every FBI employee. The group claimed it stole 2 to 3 terabytes of data related to FBI workers using a new Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability. The report also said a 24-year-old Amsterdam man, Pepijn van der Stap, was arrested on September 15, days before ShinyHunters announced the FBI jobs website breach.

findings.title: Detained ShinyHunters hacker reportedly helping FBI track down fellow members
findings.summary_md: Help Net Security reported that Saif al-Din Khader, known as Rey, was detained in Jordan and was walking investigators through his devices and digital correspondence. The FBI declined to comment on the arrest but said it had already worked with partners to arrest multiple subjects in the ShinyHunters investigation.

findings.title: FBI Blames Contractor's Missed Patch for ShinyHunters Breach
findings.summary_md: SecurityWeek reported that the FBI removed an Accenture contractor after an intrusion exposed personal information of thousands of bureau employees. The bureau blamed the contractor for failing to apply an available security patch, according to Reuters.

findings.title: Former ShinyHunters-affiliated cluster O-UNC-053 moves to new INCEPTION leak site
findings.summary_md: Okta Threat Intelligence reported that organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded INCEPTION instead of the ShinyHunters site that published targets from March through September 2026. The cluster used vishing and a phishing kit to take SSO credentials and MFA factors, and Okta said the kit could not bypass phishing-resistant methods such as Okta FastPass and FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys. Okta observed ShinyHunters listings 1 to 28 days after phishing domain registration, but said it could not validate the published data or confirm who operates INCEPTION.
